title: Superposition Geometry Under Distribution Shift: Do Features Reorganize When Input Distribution Changes?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible: if superposition geometry shifts under distribution change, SAE-based monitors calibrated on one domain degrade silently. Relevant caveat for deployment but indirect safety impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: requires understanding superposition theory, working with the Elhage et al. toy model, and conducting domain-specific SAE analysis. Comparing toy model predictions to empirical results adds theoretical depth beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multi-domain SAE feature extraction, polysemanticity scoring, plus toy model replication/comparison creates sustained effort. Each analysis step is substantial. Tight for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: While superposition geometry is being actively studied theoretically (spectral theory, correlation effects), the specific question of how superposition geometry reorganizes under distribution shift has not been directly addressed. Existing work studies static geometry given particular data statistics, but does not track the dynamic reorganization when the input distribution changes at inference time. The safety-relevant question of whether SAE monitors degrade under distribution shift due to geometric reorganization is mostly novel.

evidence.source: From Data Statistics to Feature Geometry: How Correlations Shape Superposition (2026)
evidence.finding: Studies how data correlations shape superposition geometry, showing that realistic correlated features produce anisotropic superposition rather than the polytope structure predicted by uncorrelated models.

evidence.source: Spectral Superposition: A Theory of Feature Geometry (2026)
evidence.finding: Develops a spectral theory of feature geometry in superposition, providing mathematical framework for understanding how features are organized in representational space.

evidence.source: Understanding SAE Scaling in the Presence of Feature Manifolds (2025)
evidence.finding: Studies how SAEs behave when features form manifolds rather than discrete directions, relevant to understanding feature geometry under changing distributions.
